title: Best Travel Systems (Prams and Pushchairs) UK
short: Eight travel systems tested by parents over weeks to months, compared on ride, storage, comfort and how well they cope with rough terrain.
intro: A travel system combines a carrycot, pushchair seat and often a car seat into one set that lasts from newborn to toddler, and the right one depends on your terrain, boot space and budget. This guide is based on Mumsnet's tested roundup (updated September 2026), built on over 100 hours of research, input from RoSPA and NCT groups, Which? lab test results, and hands-on testing by parent-testers who used each system in daily life for weeks or months, scoring safety and stability, assembly, ease of use, comfort, cleaning, materials and value. Prices shown are RRPs or bundle prices quoted by Mumsnet and vary by bundle.

products.name: Core 2
products.best_for: Families who want one stylish pushchair to handle pavements, parks and muddy paths from birth to toddlerhood
products.key_spec: Birth to 25kg, lie-flat seat from birth, 10kg basket, 11.7kg chassis and seat, parent and world facing
products.summary: Mumsnet's Best Buy. Over five weeks of testing it proved equally capable on pavements, cobbled streets, parks and muddy paths, feeling lighter and easier to manoeuvre than its sturdy build suggests. Tester Kate said she was 'struggling to find much I don't like' and would recommend it to her mum friends. It sits at the pricier end, the one-handed fold takes practice, the carrycot doesn't fold flat, and the car seat can be fiddly to remove.
pros: Excellent suspension for a smooth ride on all terrain
Easy to steer and manoeuvre, lightweight yet sturdy
cons: Car seat can be fiddly to remove

products.name: Atom
products.best_for: Parents starting out who want a full travel system with car seat for around £400
products.key_spec: Birth to 22kg, folds with seat unit attached (lie-flat and upright), 9kg pushchair, i-Size Cirrus car seat with ISOFIX base
products.summary: Mumsnet's tester Alice used it over eight weeks with her newborn son. She found the Cirrus car seat lighter than others she'd used, making it easier to move between cars, and the pushchair's compact fold worked in both lie-flat and upright modes, unlike bulkier systems such as the Mamas & Papas Ocarro 2 or UPPAbaby Vista V3. The under-seat basket is small at 3kg but has a flexible pull-down side. Sunshade coverage on the car seat is limited and shoulder padding is thin.
pros: Easy car seat transfer between cars
cons: Limited sunshade coverage on the car seat

products.name: Mixx Next
products.best_for: Parents who want a Which? Best Buy with excellent all-terrain wheels and a compact fold
products.key_spec: Birth to 22kg, machine-washable seat, one-handed 5-position recline, height-adjustable handlebar, 4.5kg basket
products.summary: A Which? Best Buy and one of its top-scoring pushchairs in lab tests. Mumsnet found it easy to steer, even one-handed, with durable rubber wheels and improved suspension that tackles gravel or snow. It self-stands and folds more compactly than the original Mixx. It's heavy, needs two hands to fold, and the sun hood is a little noisy to extend.
pros: Good longevity and Which? Best Buy status
Accessible storage basket, comfortable well-padded seat
Easy to switch between parent- and world-facing modes
cons: Sun hood is a little noisy to extend

products.name: Orange 4
products.badge: Best for a newborn and toddler
products.best_for: Growing families who may want to convert to a double or twin pushchair
products.key_spec: Birth to 25kg, 64L / 10kg basket, integrated ride-on buggy board, 30+ configurations, 12.1kg
products.summary: Mumsnet's tester Laura described it as looking sophisticated yet chunky, with a breathable seat and plush fur liner. It converts into a double or twin pushchair with 30+ configurations, has puncture-proof wheels and four-wheel suspension, and includes an integrated ride-on board for an older sibling. Laura found the five-point harness fiddly with a wriggly toddler, and at 12.1kg it's heavy to lift into a boot.
pros: Complete travel system that converts to a double or twin
Large carrycot suitable for overnight sleeping
Integrated ride-on buggy board for older children
cons: A little heavy to lift and carry
Takes up a lot of boot space

products.name: Wow 3
products.best_for: Parents who want a true all-in-one setup with car seat, carrycot and accessories included
products.key_spec: Birth to 22kg (about 4 years), reversible seat, includes Acorn 2 i-Size car seat and rotating base in the Everything Bundle, 11.9kg
products.summary: Mumsnet's tester Tina used the Everything Bundle daily for three months with her newborn on pavements, public transport, grass and gravel. She found a good balance between size and sturdiness, slim enough for buses yet robust enough for parks and uneven pavements, with smooth, confidence-inspiring steering, though it's not built for extreme all-terrain use. The storage basket is a little small and it's quite heavy at 11.9kg.
pros: Good value for money with loads of accessories included
Car seat has a 'good' ADAC safety rating
cons: Storage basket is a little small

products.name: Ocarro 2
products.best_for: Families in rural settings or who love outdoor adventures with their baby
products.key_spec: Birth to 22kg, overnight-sleep-approved carrycot, removable newborn liner, four-point suspension, 13.9kg
products.summary: Mumsnet's tester Rebecca used it with her eight-month-old and scored it 95/100, saying 'I would 100% recommend this pram.' Tested on pavements, grass, country paths and gravel, the suspension absorbed bumps well enough that her baby often stayed asleep. She praised its small turning circle and manageable kerbs. It's heavier than many city strollers at 13.9kg, so less ideal for stairs or crowded public transport, and the five-point harness is stiff.
pros: Dual suspension and a padded seat with newborn liner
Chunky, puncture-resistant tyres with reflective trim

products.name: Fox 5 Renew
products.best_for: Parents who regularly walk muddy paths, gravel roads or woodland trails
products.key_spec: Birth to 22kg (about 4 years), advanced four-wheel suspension, large puncture-proof wheels, recycled materials, 12.3kg
products.summary: Mumsnet's tester Beccy, reviewing the original Fox 5 that this model builds on, said it 'tackles any terrain you throw at it, from muddy paths to gravel roads and even woodland trails' and called it excellently built, sturdy and stylish yet lightweight and easy to fold. The Renew adds recycled aluminium and fabrics and a breathable mattress. It's costly, the same frame is used for carrycot and seat, no footmuff is included, and it's stiff when first assembled.
cons: Same frame used for carrycot and seat
Footmuff not included, and stiff when first assembled

products.name: Vista V3
products.best_for: Families who want the biggest storage basket and the option to add a second child later
products.key_spec: Birth (with carrycot) to 22kg, 13.6kg basket, overnight-approved carrycot, adapts to a double, 12.4kg
products.summary: Mumsnet's tester Emma, a new mum, loved how spacious it felt, saying the carrycot was roomy enough for her son 'whilst giving a safe and' secure space. It has improved suspension and puncture-proof tyres for a smooth ride on city streets and country paths, a roomy toddler seat with a higher backrest and longer footrest, and converts to a double or takes a buggy board. It's heavy and bulky when folded.
pros: Excellent storage with a huge basket
Includes carrycot for newborns, simple one-handed recline

guide.a: A lot if you use stairs, public transport or a small car boot. The Ickle Bubba Atom at 9kg is the lightest here and was praised for public transport use, while the Nuna Mixx Next (13.1kg) and Mamas & Papas Ocarro 2 (13.9kg) are heavier and better suited to a car-based routine.

guide.q: Which travel system is best for rough or muddy terrain?
guide.a: Mumsnet's testers rated the Bugaboo Fox 5 Renew and Mamas & Papas Ocarro 2 highly for all-terrain use, both handling gravel, grass and uneven paths with good suspension. The iCandy Core 2 and Cosatto Wow 3 also coped well with parks and cobbles, though the Wow 3 isn't built for extreme off-road use.

guide.q: What comes in a travel system bundle?
guide.a: This varies hugely. The Ickle Bubba Atom and Cosatto Wow 3 include a car seat and base as part of the bundle for a more complete package, while the Nuna Mixx Next and Bugaboo Fox 5 are sold with adapters for separately bought car seats. Check exactly what's included before comparing prices.

guide.q: Will I need a bigger pushchair for a second child?
guide.a: The iCandy Orange 4 and UPPAbaby Vista V3 are designed to convert into a double or twin pushchair, or take a buggy board, making them worth considering if you're planning ahead. Most other systems here are single pushchairs, though the iCandy Orange 4 also has an integrated ride-on board for an older sibling.
